en: The amihan brings cool, dry air from Siberia to the Philippines between November and February.
Mount Mayon in Albay is a perfect stratovolcano that frequently produces dangerous pyroclastic flows.
Semirara Island in Antique produces most of the Philippines' coal from compressed ancient plant fossils.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features an eight-kilometer underground waterway flowing directly into the sea.
Volcanic ash from Mount Pinatubo weathered into fertile andosol soil, boosting Baguio's vegetable harvests.
The Valley Fault System stretches across Metro Manila, requiring strict building codes to prevent earthquake damage.
Because the Philippines lies near the equator, stargazers in Batanes can observe both northern and southern constellations.
Fishermen in Manila Bay use the gravitational pull of the full moon to predict high tides.
Warm Pacific Ocean waters fuel typhoons like Rolly, causing heavy rainfall and strong winds in Luzon.
Zambales province contains large chromite ore deposits, which are mined to extract the metal chromium.
High humidity in Davao City occurs because intense tropical sunlight rapidly evaporates seawater into the atmosphere.
The Diwata-2 microsatellite, built by Filipino scientists, orbits Earth to monitor local weather and crop health.
